subject: Draft: Org update, OKR alignment & QBR talking points
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Draft: Org update, OKR alignment & QBR talking points

Team —

Ahead of next week's leadership sync and the QBR with two customer pilots, I want to align on three related items and get quick edits on the company-wide communication draft attached. High-level asks below; please reply with edits inline or send a short audio note if easier.

1) Org adjustments (proposal): consolidate Product Growth and GTM Platform into a single Growth org led by a VP-level role (temporary title: VP, Growth & Platform). Rationale: simplify cross-functional ownership of acquisition, activation, and model-cost optimization.

2) Role moves: recommend promoting Sofia (Growth PM) to Sr PM, reassigning one Senior SWE from Infra to Growth (6-month rotation), and creating a new Head of Partner Programs role (start: Q2).

3) OKR alignment for Q2 & QBR: we need 2-3 tight slides showing OKR deltas, top risks, and the proposed org changes' impact on traction/cost. I sketched an outline in the attached QBR_presentation_outline.pdf.

Please focus on clarity over diplomacy — this announcement will be read by engineers and revenue leaders alike. I want the comms to: 1) explain why (business/OKR tie-in), 2) set expectations for handover timelines, and 3) list owners for open questions (hiring, payroll, onboarding).

Draft timeline: internal leader review by EOD Monday (02/16), exec sign-off Tuesday, company email Wednesday (02/18) right after leadership town.

Attachments: 2026_Q2_org_comm_draft.docx (company announcement draft), QBR_presentation_outline.pdf

Thanks —
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales & GTM Strategy
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft: Org update, OKR alignment & QBR talking points

Karthik —

Thanks for the clear framing. A few quick thoughts after a skim:

- Opening paragraph: call out cost-per-inference and time-to-integration as the two measurable levers the reorg targets. That will help managers link to existing OKRs.
- Handover windows: add a short bullet on what 'rotation' means for the infra engineer (on-call coverage, backlog ownership during rotation).
- Comms tone: prefer "realignment" vs. "reorg" in the first line to reduce churn anxiety.

Inline (short) edits: see comments in the attached doc. Biggest add: propose a 'migration playbook' owner: Evelyn (can you confirm if you can own the playbook?).

I'll also pull the latest hiring plan numbers for Headcount Forecast (will attach before Monday).

Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, People Operations
Redwood Inference

Cc: tara@acme.com
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 12:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft: Org update, OKR alignment & QBR talking points

Karthik / Laura —

I reviewed the QBR outline and added a recommended slide that shows the expected unit-economics change from the proposed org shift (rough estimate: 7-10% lower per-inference spend due to tighter model-routing + dedicated batching experiments). I attached a short table in the deck.

One operational ask: if we announce to the company on 02/18, can we commit to one-week transition windows per team to avoid sprint disruption? If that's not feasible, let's be explicit about which teams have two-week windows.

On the external front, Tara from Acme asked for a brief heads-up call before our QBR — I CC'd her to align on logistics (she's fine with a 20-min preview call). I don't think we should give partner-specific details, but offering a high-level signal that we're aligning GTM to cost/scale is fine.

-Ava
Ava Chen
Director, Product Management (GTM)
Redwood Inference

Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 15:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft: Org update, OKR alignment & QBR talking points

Karthik —

I can own the migration playbook. I'll put together a two-page checklist (tech handoffs, runbook ownership, monitoring thresholds to adjust) and share it by Monday morning. A few specifics I want to confirm:

- Will the infra engineer rotation keep primary on-call until fully ramped? If so, we need a clear escalation path documented in the playbook.
- For the partner programs head, do we expect a vendor/market-facing resume (external hire) or an internal promotion? If internal, Marcus and I can draft an internal job brief.

I'll also add an ops slide to the QBR outline showing a 30/60/90 ramp plan for any moved headcount.

Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Head of Platform Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Draft: Org update, OKR alignment & QBR talking points

All —

Quick thank-you and a couple of clarifications from my side:

- I'm fine with the one-week transition if we allow teams to queue higher-risk migrations into the two-week bucket. I'll mark a list of likely candidates and share with Evelyn by EOD Monday.
- For the company announcement draft: suggest we include a short FAQ appendix covering payroll timing, title changes, and expected changes to compensation (if any). HR will need to sign-off. Laura — can you take the FAQ draft?
- External comm: I agree with Ava that a short pre-QBR heads-up to Acme is OK, but let's avoid sharing internal org charts. Tara (CC'd earlier) — if you want to coordinate a 20-min sync, feel free to send a few slots and we'll do our best to accommodate.

I'll go update the QBR deck with a slide showing top-3 customer asks that motivated the shift.

Marcus Lin
Director, Partner Engineering
Redwood Inference
